evidence: His official voter pamphlet statement pledges to protect Alaska's existing Medicaid expansion and expand telehealth (Jun 2026); no provider-rate plan.
Voter pamphlet vows to lower electric bills by making utilities cooperate and building renewables (Jun 2026); related but not fee caps or limits on utility lobbying.
Voter pamphlet promises cheaper child care by easing regulations on starting providers (Jun 2026); no universal child care plan.
Voter pamphlet commits to cutting red tape that blocks building more homes (Jun 2026); state-land claim in prior note not found in that statement.
Proposed a moratorium on new data centers until regulators, including the RCA on power, can protect Alaskans (Aug 2026); not a full-cost mandate.
Backs restoring a teacher retirement benefit to cut 21% turnover and wants inflation-indexed school funding (Aug-Oct 2026); no specific pay raise pledge.
State of the State touted her program erasing $642M in medical debt for about half a million people and proposed barring it from credit reports (Jan 2026).
Proposed eliminating insurer prior authorization requirements in her State of the State (Jan 2026); no insulin co-pay proposal found.
Proposed ending the $38M data center tax exemption and charging data centers the same water rate as families (Jan 2026).
Proposed a $20M Arizona Affordability Fund, paid by a short-term-rental fee, to help with utility bills (Jan 2026); aid, not a freeze.
Proposed a new Housing Acceleration Fund, seeded with $2.5M and leveraging private money, to finance more homes (Jan 2026).
State of the State called for expanded down payment help for first-time buyers (Jan 2026); no broker-fee position found.
Called her $200M-plus Middle Class Tax Cuts package, with a bigger standard deduction and no tax on tips or overtime, her top priority (Jan 2026).
Her tax package adds a $6,000 deduction for those over 65 (Jan 2026); Arizona already exempts Social Security, so this is senior relief, not that.
Warned more money for universal ESA vouchers would blow a hole in finances; wants them refocused on disabled and military kids (Jan 2026); no repeal.
Criticized federal Medicaid cuts in her State of the State (Jan 2026); Arizona already expanded, and no rate-increase plan found.
Denounced fraud and abuse in ESA voucher spending and launched an efficiency initiative to save up to $100M (Jan 2026); no inspector general plan.
Signed bipartisan bills requiring larger cities to allow casitas and middle housing like duplexes (May 2024).
Listed as a supporter of Prop 139, which wrote abortion rights into Arizona's constitution and passed with 61.6% (Nov 2024).
Pledges to strengthen Medi-Cal and reverse limits that dropped undocumented immigrants (Nov 2026); California already expanded; executive-order claim not verified.
Said he would freeze utility rates and home insurance premiums and demand transparency on rate hikes (May 2026).
Opposes suspending the gas tax, saying roads and bridges need the money, and dismisses 33-cent relief (Oct 2026); no halving pledge found.
Vows to declare a housing emergency on day one and finance about 40,000 shovel-ready units (May 2026).
Says the wealthy should pay their fair share but opposes the billionaire wealth tax and hasn't endorsed new income taxes (Nov 2026); Prop 55 claim unverified.
Campaign priorities pledge to expand help with child care costs (2026); no universal child care plan.
Backs expanding SB 79 transit upzoning and SB 684, and a 90-day deadline for local permit decisions, per CA YIMBY's endorsement (Jun 2026).
Promised to enforce new state laws limiting immigration agents' use of force and activity on state property (Nov 2026); not a sensitive-locations ban.
Wants to pay for health programs partly by cutting administrative spending, waste and fraud, without specifics (Aug 2026).
Signed the LEARNS Act creating Arkansas's universal school voucher program (Mar 2023).
Signed the LEARNS Act, which raised the minimum starting teacher salary (Mar 2023).
Signed special-session acts cutting individual and corporate income taxes (May 2026); broad cuts, not targeted at the middle class.
Signed Act 548, lowering the threshold for data centers' sales tax exemption from $500M to $100M and extending it to expansions (Apr 2025).
Pushed and signed presumptive Medicaid eligibility for pregnant women (Feb 2025) but called a 12-month postpartum extension duplicative.
His policy playbook says he would not expand Medicaid, seeking federal rural health aid and flexibility instead (Oct 2026).
Playbook would end data center tax breaks, tax them in the top property class and make developers pay for power lines and water (Oct 2026).
Playbook pledges to extend the utility base-rate freeze (Oct 2026).
Would shield residential customers from grid costs driven by big industrial users (Oct 2026); not fee caps or limits on utility lobbying.
Proposes freezing property-tax increases on senior-occupied homes, worked out with counties (Oct 2026).
Family Affordability Act would cut income taxes in steps and end the grocery tax (Oct 2026); broad cuts, not targeted at the middle class.
Would phase child care aid down gradually to avoid benefit cliffs and grow provider and employer tax credits (Oct 2026); no universal plan.
Pledges to fully fund First Class Pre-K, aiming for a seat for every family that wants one in his first term (Oct 2026).
Would let experienced teachers earn more by mentoring colleagues in high-need middle schools (Oct 2026); no across-the-board raise.
Playbook backs the CHOOSE Act, Alabama's education savings account voucher program (Oct 2026).
Commits to greater state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement (Oct 2026); no specific stance on sensitive locations.
Proposes agency audits, independently verified savings and stepped-up Medicaid fraud enforcement (Oct 2026).
Governor playbook pledges tighter limits on abortion pills mailed into Alabama (Oct 2026).
